when: asm is byte-identical to the target except register names (a pure regalloc miss), and a u8/u16 param feeds two or more use sites
rule: cache the param in a u32 local first: `u32 c = count;` then use `c` everywhere. Forces MWCC to the matching allocation. Fixed GXSetNumChans 47->100%.

when: the function is a thin wrapper that only calls one other same-file function, and the target has a real `bl` (a stack frame + branch) but yours inlined it
rule: bracket the function with `#pragma dont_inline on` / `#pragma dont_inline reset`. MWCC auto-inlines small same-TU callees. Fixed GXSetTevDirect, __GXSetVCD.

when: the diff shows a `clrlwi/clrrwi` + `rlwimi` pair where the wrong operand is the accumulator (clr'd side)
rule: in `(A & maskA) | (B & maskB)` the SECOND operand becomes the rlwimi accumulator (gets clr'd, keeps its bits); the first gets inserted. Swap operand order to flip it. GXLoadTlut needed `(field & high) | (val & low)` for 100%; wrong order = 89.7%.

when: target uses a single `rlwimi` (bitfield insert) but your GX_SET_REG/GX_BITFIELD_SET emitted `rlwinm`+`or` (AND-OR)
rule: replace the macro with a direct `__rlwimi(field, value, shift, mb, me)`. GX_SET_REG is AND-OR; GX_SET_TRUNC / __rlwimi is the insert form. Match whichever the target uses.

when: several consecutive bitfield inserts into the same reg
rule: write them as ONE nested expression `r = __rlwimi(__rlwimi(__rlwimi(reg,b,..),c,..),d,..)` after an in-place first insert. Separate self-assign statements emit stray `mr`/copy instructions. GXTev In fns matched this way.

when: the value is a sum of ternary bools like `(x?1:0)+(y?1:0)+...`
rule: accumulate progressively: `n = t0 + t1; n = n + t2; n = n + t3; ...`. One big expression OR one-var-per-bool both mismatch the add/regalloc order. Fixed __GXXfVtxSpecs.

when: a global flag (gx->dirtyState, gx->tcsManEnab, etc.) is tested/used more than once
rule: RE-READ it from memory before each use; never cache it in a local. The target reloads it each time. Fixed __GXSetDirtyState/GXBegin/GXSetCullMode.

when: the target stores a field with `sth` (halfword) or `stb` (byte) but yours used `stw` (word), or vice-versa
rule: the store width IS the field type: stb=u8, sth=u16, stw=u32. Change the struct field type to match. GXTlutObj.numEntries was u32 -> u16 (target uses sth). Full-build after a shared-struct change.

when: the target's stack frame is larger than yours (stwu with a bigger negative offset) with no matching locals
rule: add an unused local like `u8 unused[8];` to grow the frame to match. DEBUG-only/unused locals still consume slots. Load-bearing in GXSetViewportJitter (frame 0x60).

when: you need the real algorithm/struct for an SDK function (GX*, OS*, JSystem)
rule: this SDK matches camthesaxman/smb-decomp era, NOT zeldaret/tp (tp is a NEWER SDK — e.g. its GXSetViewport calls __GXSetViewport which does not exist here). Also check pikmin2, ac-decomp. GitHub code-search the mangled or demangled symbol.

when: an m2c machine-decompiled draft is present in this packet
rule: trust its CONTROL FLOW and which struct offsets/bits move (it is derived from the real asm); do NOT trust its type names or unkNN field names. Rewrite to project style but keep the branch/expression shape.

when: clearing bits of a reg before setting
rule: write masked updates as expressions `reg & ~X | Y`, not as separate reassignment statements — the latter emit extra instructions.

when: the diff is only register-naming / a base pointer like `gx + i*4` is recomputed in the target but CSE'd (computed once) in yours
rule: this is instruction scheduling / regalloc, not a source bug. Try the cache-u8-in-u32 trick or temp reordering; if it resists, it is permuter territory — schedule `forge/permute-fn.py`.

when: objdiff 2.7.1 shows a data_value diff of 100 or the code is byte-perfect but a later literal-pool offset is shifted
rule: an EARLIER unmatched stub in the same TU failed to emit its string, shifting @stringBase offsets. Not fixable from this function — match the owning stub first. Skip; not a real target.
